skill.name: golang-spf13-cobra
skill.description: Golang CLI command tree library using spf13/cobra — cobra.Command, RunE vs Run, PersistentPreRunE hook chain, Args validators (NoArgs, ExactArgs, MatchAll, custom), persistent vs local flags, command groups, ValidArgsFunction, RegisterFlagCompletionFunc, ShellCompDirective, usage/help template customization, man-page and markdown doc generation, and testing with SetArgs/SetOut/SetErr. Apply when using or adopting spf13/cobra, or when the codebase imports `github.com/spf13/cobra`. For configuration layering alongside cobra, see the `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-spf13-viper` skill. For general CLI architecture (project layout, exit codes, signal handling, I/O patterns), see `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-cli`.
skill.summary: Design, implement, test, and review Go CLI command trees with spf13/cobra.
skill.author: samber

content.value_statement: Go CLI projects often become inconsistent around command structure, validation, hooks, output, and tests. This skill provides practical Cobra patterns for predictable commands and maintainable test suites.
actual_capabilities: Design root commands, subcommands, groups, local flags, and persistent flags.
Select RunE hooks and compose PersistentPreRunE, PreRunE, and PostRunE behavior.
Apply built-in and custom positional argument validators with MatchAll.
Configure static and dynamic shell completions with Cobra directives.
Generate command documentation and customize help or usage templates.
Test commands with isolated trees, captured output, error paths, and completions.
limitations: It does not implement application business logic or external API clients.
It does not replace official Cobra or pflag version documentation.
It does not provide full CLI architecture, deployment, or signal-handling guidance.
Dynamic completions still require the application to define safe data access.

use_cases.title: Create a New CLI
use_cases.description: Define a root command, organize subcommands, add flags, validate arguments, and return errors consistently.
use_cases.target_user: Go developers starting a command-line application

use_cases.title: Extend an Existing CLI
use_cases.description: Add commands, completion behavior, configuration hooks, or generated documentation while preserving the existing command tree.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainers working in an established Go repository

use_cases.title: Review Command Quality
use_cases.description: Audit hook ordering, output writers, argument validation, flag state, and test isolation for common Cobra mistakes.
use_cases.target_user: Engineers reviewing or refactoring Go CLI code

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Run Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: I am adding a Go Cobra subcommand that calls an API. Explain whether Run or RunE is appropriate, and show the error flow.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Command Arguments
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cobra delete command that accepts exactly one resource name. Use the correct Args validator and explain the resulting user error.

prompt_templates.title: Add Testable Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cobra command handler and update its output approach so tests can capture standard output and errors without using process-global streams.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Command Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Go Cobra command tree for hook inheritance, flag scope, completion safety, argument validation, documentation generation, and test isolation. List concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: A command needs one valid resource argument and should reject unknown names before its handler runs.
output_examples.output: Use Cobra argument validation before the handler. Combine an exact-argument rule with a valid-argument rule, then access the validated resource in the handler.

output_examples.input: A test passes after setting a port, but a later test unexpectedly keeps the earlier port.
output_examples.output: The tests reuse a command tree whose flag state persists. Build a fresh root command and subcommand tree for each test case.

output_examples.input: A CLI needs completion for output formats and must prevent unrelated file suggestions.
output_examples.output: Register a flag completion function that returns the allowed formats and disables file completion for this exhaustive value list.

best_practices: Use RunE and return errors instead of exiting inside command handlers.
Write command output through Cobra-provided writers so tests can capture it.
Create a fresh command tree for each test to prevent state leakage.
anti_patterns: Do not validate positional argument counts manually inside RunE.
Do not define a child PersistentPreRunE without preserving required parent setup.
Do not treat shell completion callbacks as a substitute for command authorization.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when building, extending, or reviewing a Go CLI that imports spf13/cobra.

faq.question: Does it cover Viper configuration?
faq.answer: It explains Cobra integration boundaries and points configuration layering to the related Viper skill.

faq.question: Why prefer RunE over Run?
faq.answer: RunE returns errors through Cobra. Run cannot return errors and encourages process exits or panics in handlers.

faq.question: How should command tests handle output?
faq.answer: Use Cobra output writers and redirect them to buffers. This keeps tests deterministic and avoids process-global streams.

faq.question: How do I avoid flag state leaking between tests?
faq.answer: Construct a new command tree for every test case instead of reusing one command instance.

faq.question: Can it generate CLI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Markdown, YAML, RST, and man-page generation, plus help and usage template customization.
